messages:
Danielle: FYI Parklane Health dispute: INV-2029-045 includes full April platform fee but they claim customer-facing outage Mar 22-29 during our private deployment migration. They want a credit.
Maria: Can you drop the invoice line items and the customer's outage report here? Need to confirm dates and amounts.
Danielle: Invoice shows: PLATFORM_FEE $12,500; SUPPORT_TIER Enterprise $4,000; USAGE $3,200. Customer email: 'We were unable to serve inference traffic from 22-29 Mar. Multiple retries failed, app-level 503s.' Attached screenshots.
BillingBot: Invoice INV-2029-045 posted 1857505000. Billing period 2029-04-01 to 2029-04-30.
OpsBot: Migration for Parklane executed 2029-03-20 -> initial completion. Incident 2029-03-24 14:05 UTC: rollback and node restarts. Pager duration 6h. Post-migration logs show increased restart rate Mar 24-26 but platform metrics show healthy by Mar 27.
Nate: Customer ticket TKT-7831 contains their app logs showing failures through Mar 29 at 09:00 local. We have overlapping symptoms but need to attribute root cause (our migration vs their infra).
Alex: Legal: clause 5.2 Service Credits applies when unavailability >72h and attributable to Redwood. We need documented attribution to apply contractual credits.
Sanjay: Business perspective: Parklane is strategic and up for renewal in Q3. Offering a conciliatory credit may avoid churn. Suggest pro-rata platform fee for affected days + partial support credit.
Maria: Compute options: pro-rata for 8 affected days = (8/30)*12,500 = $3,333.33. Full month credit = $12,500. Support options: waive full $4k for April, or 50% ($2k). Finance recommends cap at $6k total without CFO OK.
Danielle: Customer first asks for pro-rata platform fee + full support waiver = $3,333 + $4,000 = $7,333.
Elaine: I can approve up to $6,000 credit for relationship retention but need sign-off recorded. Provide PR code and email acceptance.
Maria: Proposed counteroffer: PLATFORM_CREDIT -$3,333 (pro rata), SUPPORT_CREDIT -$2,000 (50% of April), TOTAL -$5,333. Will include acceptance clause that this settles outage claim for Mar 22-29.
Danielle: Sounds fair. I'll confirm with Parklane if they accept 50% support waiver. If they push back, escalate to Elaine for final approval.
BillingBot: To apply credit, create credit memo CM-2029-178. Auto-check: CM > $5,000 requires CFO approval code.
Sanjay: If customer insists on full support waiver, alternative is to split refund over two invoices to reduce cashflow hit but still satisfy them.
Alex: Legal: include release language: 'Customer accepts credited amount as full and final settlement for the specified outage period and waives further claims for that period.' We should capture their explicit reply.
Danielle: I'll draft the settlement email and copy Legal and Finance. Draft text: 'We apologize for the disruption. As goodwill, Redwood will apply a $5,333 credit to INV-2029-045 to cover a pro-rated platform fee and partial support waiver, contingent on your written acceptance that this resolves claims for Mar 22-29.'
Elaine: Approve PR-2029-PARK-61 for up to $6,000. Record in audit.
Maria: Creating CM-2029-178 now with lines: -PLATFORM_CREDIT -$3,333; -SUPPORT_CREDIT -$2,000; Total -$5,333. Comment: Approved PR-2029-PARK-61 (Elaine).
BillingBot: CM-2029-178 created and attached to INV-2029-045. Status: pending customer acceptance.
Danielle: Sending settlement email to Parklane now. Will update thread with their reply and close TKT-7831 once accepted.
Nate: Adding ticket link and diagnostic bundle to invoice audit trail per Elaine's request.
Maria: Thanks team. Note for records: if customer rejects, escalate to Elaine for final approval of up to full month credit.
